turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

Test input (2x19):
6 6 7 7 7 7 6 7 7 0 4 4 4 4 6 6 4 6 6
7 7 7 6 6 7 7 7 6 0 4 6 4 6 4 4 4 4 4
Wrong attempts used: 0/8. Demo requests used: 0/8.
Reply with exactly one action JSON on the last line.

Local continual harness entries belong to this Prime Agent session. Global continual harness entries persist across Prime Agent sessions.
The continual harness entries below are compact summaries, not full descriptions. Use them as routing/context hints; inspect or refine the underlying continual harness entry only when detail matters.

Keep `await refine.run()` continual harness edits small and evidence-backed.

Spawn a continual harness subagent spec by composing a concise task prompt and calling `handle = await rlm.spawn('sub-task', name='worker')`; admission returns immediately with `rlm_child_id`, `name`, `session_dir`, and `model`, never the child's answer. Results arrive only through explicit `agent_message` replies or files; children reply with `await agent_message.send(message, receiver_role='parent')`. Use `await rlm.list_subagents()` to recover direct child handles and `await agent_message.send(..., receiver_role='child', receiver_name=handle.name)` for follow-ups. Do not invent wrappers such as `call_skill(...)`, `run_subagent(...)`, or named subagent registries.

[('arc_fill_gaps_between_aligned_markers', 'ARC: fill gaps between aligned markers', 'Continual-ARC task-0e26539b (confirmed by a correct submission): On a grid with background color and marker pixels (demo: background 1, markers 6; prior test: background 7, markers 8; another test: background 9, markers 0), keep every marker unchanged and fill background cells with color 3 when they lie strictly between two markers on the same row or column. Apply across each aligned marker interval; cells outside those intervals stay background. Checking adjacent markers in sorted row/column order is sufficient because the union of intervals between any pair equals the union of intervals between consecutive markers. Example: three markers in one column at rows 1, 2, and 5 cause rows 3-4 between the latter pair to become 3. Additional confirmed demo evidence: with background 4 and marker 9, all strictly-between cells on aligned rows/columns become 3 (not 9); e.g. row 0 markers at columns 10 and 13 fill columns 11-12 with 3, and row 2 markers at columns 1 and 12 fill columns 2-11 with 3. A lone marker (demo: background 6, marker 8) remains unchanged. In test background 2/marker 0, the gap likewise became 3; filling it with 0 was incorrect. Rule: fill only cells that were background and lie in a row/column interval bracketed by at least two markers; preserve marker pixels. Latest confirmed test (background 9, markers 1) also followed the same rule: row intervals included r3 c7–15, r8 c12–18; vertical markers in column 11 at rows 2, 5, and 7 filled intervening rows 3–4 and 6. A marker pair at r7 c10–11 is adjacent and adds no cells. The successful output confirms fill color 3 and the union-of-horizontal-and-vertical intervals.'), ('arc_color_the_trailing_gap_after_a_horizontal_marker_row', 'ARC: color the trailing gap after a horizontal marker row', 'Continual-ARC task-b4235fd4. Fill color is always 1; background and marker colors vary. Core rule: for each intended multirow marker-pattern group, identify its rightmost marker extent. Color the trailing background suffix to the right edge only on rows with a horizontal marker run reaching that group’s rightmost extent; preserve marker pixels and all other cells. Do NOT treat every isolated 8-connected island inside a dense patterned band as its own fill target: that causes large overfills. Likewise, a lone marker at the maximum column in a row is not enough if it does not form the horizontal marker run (confirmed current test: lower 4x22 pattern has max marker col20; rows21 and23 have horizontal 4-runs ending at c20, so only their c21 cells become 1; rows22 and24 have isolated c20 markers and remain unchanged. Upper band ends at c21, so has no trailing suffix). This exact output solved the current test on the third submission after (wrong) attempts that independently filled 8-connected islands and then filled c21 on all four lower rows.

Confirmed demos: (1) bg2/fg0, row0 run c0-2 and trailing suffix c3-8 -> 1; full marker rows with no trailing space unchanged. (2) bg0/fg6, upper group max c9 reached by row1 -> fill c10-14 only; lower group max c12 reached by row8 -> fill c13-14. (3) bg5/fg2, row0’s rightmost horizontal run c7-8 ends at c8 -> c9-10 become 1; the later group had marker at far edge and stayed unchanged. (4) bg0/fg2, top group has rightmost marker c17 in rows0-2 -> c18-19 become 1 in all three; lower group reaches edge c19 and stays unchanged. (5) bg4/fg9, upper group reaches edge c17 and stays unchanged; lower group has rightmost c12, rows15 and17 horizontal runs to c12 and fill c13-17. In that demo row16 also had c13,c15,c17 changed to 1 while even c14,c16 remained bg; preserve as observed, not fully explained by the simple rule. Another earlier demo with bg4/fg9 changed only row0 c28 (between a final 9 marker at c27 and 4 at c29); indicates avoid assuming all pattern objects have simple one-color backgrounds.

Past failure: my first attempt used 8-connected components and filled suffixes after each island, causing overfill. My second attempt colored c21 on all four rows of the lower band; only rows with a horizontal run to the group max were eligible. Prefer grouping the visually coherent multirow pattern and applying the rightmost-horizontal-run criterion; preserve all unrelated pixels.

(6) New confirmed test (task-b4235fd4; bg9/fg8; 29x11): top group rows0-2 has row0 singleton marker at c2 and rows1-2 markers c0-1; correct output colors row0 c3-10 with 1, leaving the other rows unchanged. Lower group rows12-14 has a full horizontal marker row c2-10 reaching the right edge, so no suffix is added. Thus a singleton can qualify when it is the leading/rightmost row of this multirow pattern group (do not apply the isolated-marker exclusion without considering its role in the group). Initial all-unchanged submission was wrong; one demo confirmed the fill color 1 and suffix rule. Demo examples showed groups like rows3-4 and 7-8 with horizontal runs reaching edge unchanged, while a final group row16 c2-3 was filled c4-8.'), ('arc_compare_two_binary_panels_at_their_shared_color', 'ARC: compare two binary panels at their shared color', 'Continual-ARC task-638c72af (confirmed correct on multiple recurrences). A uniform separator row or column divides the grid into two equal-sized panels; omit it and compare cells at identical coordinates. Each panel is binary; let S be the single color shared by both panels. Output has one panel’s dimensions, is filled with color 3, and uses S at each coordinate where EITHER corresponding input cell is not S. Equivalently: output 3 only where BOTH corresponding cells equal S; otherwise output S. Do not reverse these output colors. Examples: demo with S=9 outputs 3 at common-background locations, 9 where either panel has a non-9 speckle. Confirmed test with upper colors {8,1}, lower {1,4}, separator row [0,0], S=1; compare top rows 0–13 to input rows 15–28. Correct output: [[1,1],[1,3],[1,3],[1,1],[1,3],[1,1],[1,1],[3,1],[1,1],[3,1],[1,1],[1,3],[1,3],[1,1]]. Careful: bottom panel starts immediately after separator (row 15 in this 0-indexed 29x2 case); map all 14 rows in order.')]
